label: def:archimedean-condition
title: Descartes condition
html:
A quantum observable universe (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) over R (quantum observable universe, QU-to-QOU lifting) satisfies the Descartes condition if the base curve M_0 of its archimedean realisation has genus four,

  g(M_0) = 4, \qquad \text{equivalently} \qquad \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) = -6 .

This requires 6 \in R^{\times} (i.e. \mathrm{char}(R) \nmid 6). By QU-to-QOU lifting(3--4), this forces \kappa_n \neq 0 for all n and produces 6 branch points in the geometric descent (with total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2d + 6). A quantum observable universe satisfying this condition is called a Descartes universe.

The condition is a statement about the base, not about the substrate object. The number \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) is the topological Euler characteristic of a curve (the three Euler characteristics); the categorical trace \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = \dim_q(A) is a different quantity and does not enter the condition.
